Report DescriptionPOSSIBLE, UNCONFIRMED OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. REPORT DATE: 08-13-2026 REPORT TIME: 1042 UTC REGION: GULF OF AMERICA SUB REGION: N/A AREA/BLOCK: EUGENE ISLAND 316 IMAGE DATE: 08-12-2026 IMAGE TIME: 1638 UTC DATA SOURCE: SENTINEL2C MODE: MULTISPECTRAL RESOLUTION: 10 METER LOCATION: 28°15'46" N/91°37'07" W AREA: 1.53 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: HIGH REPORT MAP/GIS FILES: HTTPS://WWW.OSPO.NOAA.GOV/PRODUCTS/OCEAN/MARINEPOLLUTION/ REMARKS: POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. THE LINEAR ANOMALY WAS BELIEVED TO BE EMANATING TOWARDS THE NORTHEAST FROM AN OIL PIPELINE IN EUGENE ISLAND BLOCK 316. IT EXHIBITED SIGNIFICANT CONTRAST AGAINST THE OCEAN BACKGROUND IN OPTICAL IMAGERY, WITH A SILVERY RAINBOW SHEEN THAT EXTENDED FROM THE SOURCE FOR ALMOST HALF THE LENGTH OF THE ANOMALY, INDICATIVE OF POSSIBLE THICKER OIL. THE SEGMENT OF THICKER OIL MEASURED 1.55 NM IN LENGTH, AND IN TOTAL THE ANOMALY MEASURED APPROXIMATELY 5.2 NM IN LENGTH AND 0.18 NM AT ITS WIDEST POINT. WINDS NEAR THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WERE OUT OF THE SE AT APPROXIMATELY 10 KTS. UNCERTAINTIES: THE EXACT PIPELINE COULD NOT BE DETERMINED DUE TO THE PRESENCE OF MULTIPLE PIPELINES IN THE IMMEDIATE VICINITY. MULTIPLE REPEAT OCCURRENCES WERE PREVIOUSLY REPORTED, WITH THE MOST RECENT NOAA NESDIS RESPONSELINK REPORTS INCLUDING #1470110 (8/7) AND #1469403 (7/31).

Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** ON NOVEMBER 16, 2011, A TRUCK SUFFERED A MECHANICAL FAILURE CAUSING THE FUEL PUMP TO FAIL, WHICH RESULTED IN THE RELEASE OF APPROXIMATELY 5 GALLONS OF DIESEL FUEL ONTO THE ASPHALT PARKING LOT AND CAUSED A LIGHT SHEEN IN A NEARBY STORM DRAIN. CONTRACTOR HAS BEEN DISPATCHED TO THE SITE TO PERFORM CLEANUP OPERATIONS. ABSORBENT BOOM WAS PLACED IN FRONT OF THE NEARBY STORM DRAIN TO ENSURE NO ADDITIONAL MATERIAL IMPACTS THE DRAIN. ABSORBENTS WERE ALSO PLACED IN THE DRAIN TO COLLECT THE CONTAMINATED LIQUID. THE DRAIN VALVE WAS SHUT OFF AND THE MATERIAL WAS CONTAINED IN THE CATCH BASIN OF THE DRAIN. ABSORBENT BOOM WAS ALSO PLACED AT THE OUTFALL OF THE DRAIN WHERE A NEARBY CREEK IS AS A PRECAUTIONARY MEASURE TO COLLECT ANY POTENTIAL RESIDUAL.

Report Description
REPORTING ADDITIONAL AIR RELEASE POINTS OF AMMONIA, TO BE ADDED TO ITS CONTINUOUS AMMONIA RELEASE REPORT , CR-ERNS #965529 DATED JAN 24, 2011. NONE OF THESE ADDITIONAL AIR RELEASE POINTS ARE REPORTABLE RELEASES, SEPARATELY OR IN AGGREGATE. THIS REPORT IS TO IDENTIFY ALL AIR RELEASE POINTS OF AMMONIA AT OUR FACILITY, REGARDLESS OF SIZE. ALL OF THESE POINTS ARE CLASSIFIED AS CONTINOUS, HOWEVER THE ACTUAL RELEASE IS INTERMITTENT. BON L HAS 10 WASTEWATER TREATMENT TANKS IN ITS MAIN WWT SYSTEM THAT HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO RELEASE AMMONIA. THE ESTIMATED DAILY RELEASE OF ALL THESE TANKS IS LESS THAN 8 POUNDS OF AMMONIA PER DAY. THE AMMONIA RELEASED FROM THE MAIN WWT SYSTEM IS THE SAME SOURCE AS THE AMMONIA STRIPPER CONTINUOUS RELEASE REPORT LISTED ABOVE. BON L HAS THE FOLLOWING RELEASE POINTS ASSOICATED WITH DIFFERENT SOURCES OF AMMONIA. BON L HAS 6 TANKS IN ITS PAINT LINE WASTEWATER TREATMENT SYSTEM, WHICH CAN RELEASE RELEASE DAILY LESS THAN 5 POUNDS OF AMMONIA PER DAY. BON L HAS 2 DIE NITRIDER RELEASE POINTS, BOTH DAILY RELEASE LESS THAN A POUND PER DAY, OF AMMONIA. BON L PRODUCES A DROSS BY-PRODUCT THAT CONTAINS NITROGEN COMPOUNDS THAT IF COME IN CONTACT WITH MOISTURE CAN RELEASE TRACE AMOUNTS OF AMMONIA. THE DROSS STORAGE BIN IS ESTIMATED TO RELEASE LESS THAN 1 POUND A DAY, OF AMMONIA. LAST IS THE LAB WHICH RELEASES LESS THAN A GRAM A DAY.

NONE OF THESE ADDITIONAL AIR RELEASE POINTS ARE REPORTABLE RELEASES, SEPARATELY OR IN AGGREGATE. THIS REPORT IS TO IDENTIFY ALL AIR RELEASE POINTS OF AMMONIA AT OUR FACILITY, REGARDLESS OF SIZE. ALL OF THESE POINTS ARE CLASSIFIED AS CONTINOUS, HOWEVER THE ACTUAL RELEASE IS INTERMITTENT. BON L HAS 10 WASTEWATER TREATMENT TANKS IN ITS MAIN WWT SYSTEM THAT HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO RELEASE AMMONIA. THE ESTIMATED DAILY RELEASE OF ALL THESE TANKS IS LESS THAN 8 POUNDS OF AMMONIA PER DAY. THE AMMONIA RELEASED FROM THE MAIN WWT SYSTEM IS THE SAME SOURCE AS THE AMMONIA STRIPPER CONTINUOUS RELEASE REPORT LISTED ABOVE. BON L HAS THE FOLLOWING RELEASE POINTS ASSOICATED WITH DIFFERENT SOURCES OF AMMONIA. BON L HAS 6 TANKS IN ITS PAINT LINE WASTEWATER TREATMENT SYSTEM, WHICH CAN RELEASE RELEASE DAILY LESS THAN 5 POUNDS OF AMMONIA PER DAY. BON L HAS 2 DIE NITRIDER RELEASE POINTS, BOTH DAILY RELEASE LESS THAN A POUND PER DAY, OF AMMONIA. BON L PRODUCES A DROSS BY-PRODUCT THAT CONTAINS NITROGEN COMPOUNDS THAT IF COME IN CONTACT WITH MOISTURE CAN RELEASE TRACE AMOUNTS OF AMMONIA. THE DROSS STORAGE BIN IS ESTIMATED TO RELEASE LESS THAN 1 POUND A DAY, OF AMMONIA. LAST IS THE LAB WHICH RELEASES LESS THAN A GRAM A DAY.
